phone.title: How to Use the Washer
phone.model: Whirlpool Model WFW9351 or WFW9151 (to confirm)
phone.important: Never wash anything with gasoline or other flammable fluids on it: fire risk. Use only HE (High Efficiency) detergent. Do not overload. Do not reach in while the drum moves, and do not let children play on or in the washer. Run the washer only when you are home, and never on an extension cord.
phone.stop: Water leaks. An error code comes back after a restart, or the washer will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or grinding or banging noise. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's manual W10432633A for Whirlpool front-loading washer models WFW9351 and WFW9151. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Sort by colour and fabric. Keep very dirty items and delicates apart.
Empty pockets, close zippers and hooks, tie strings. Coins can block the pump.
Load loosely, mixing large and small items. Do not wash a single item alone. Small items go in mesh bags.
Small load: 3 to 5 items (1/4 full). Medium: 1/2. Large: 3/4. Clothes must tumble freely.
Push the door until the latch clicks.
HE detergent, liquid or powder, in its compartment. Colour-safe bleach can go with it. Do not mix powder and liquid.
Fabric softener (liquid only): max 1/4 cup (60 mL), not past MAX. No softener balls.
Chlorine bleach: max 2/3 cup (165 mL), not past MAX. Never colour-safe bleach here.
Never pour products straight onto clothes.
Close the drawer slowly and fully. A little water left in it is normal.
Press and hold POWER, then turn the knob.

Normal: everyday loads. Heavy Duty: towels, jeans. Whitest Whites. Cold Wash: colours. Delicate: lingerie, sweaters. Bulky Items: comforters. Small Load: 3 to 5 items. Rinse/Drain & Spin: spin out a wet load.
Not sure? Choose Normal for everyday laundry.
Buttons under the display change Temperature, Spin and Soil Level. Faster spin means drier clothes but more wrinkles.
Extra Rinse, Delay Start (up to 10 h, use powder detergent).

TumbleFresh: keeps clean clothes from sitting still and getting musty when you can't empty the washer right away. After the wash ends, the drum turns the clothes over every now and then, for up to 6 hours. Turn it on before starting the wash: press TumbleFresh until its light comes on. While it runs, the Done light stays on, the TumbleFresh light flashes and the door stays locked. Press POWER any time to stop it and unlock the door; otherwise it stops by itself after 6 hours. It doesn't work when spin speed is set to No Spin.
Press and hold START/PAUSE. The door locks, unlocks and locks again: normal. Start within 5 minutes or it turns off.
Add 1 or 2 items while Add a Garment is lit: press START/PAUSE once, wait for the door to unlock.
Pause: press START/PAUSE once; hold it to continue. Cancel: press POWER. Lock buttons: hold Control Lock 3 s.

At the end, the Done light comes on in the display (picture below). Unload straight away and check the door seal for small items. If TumbleFresh is on, Done stays lit and the door stays locked: press POWER to unlock.

items.cap: Display on model WFW9151 (WFW9351 has the same Done light). Manual, page 6.

items.html: Leave the door open so the drum dries. Open and close it before the next wash.

phone.title: Washer Care
phone.model: Whirlpool Model WFW9351 or WFW9151 (to confirm)
phone.important: Wear rubber gloves when cleaning with bleach and follow the bleach label. Do not use abrasive cleaners, and do not take any part of the washer apart. Use only HE detergent and measure it: too much leaves residue and causes smells.
phone.stop: A water hose behind the washer is bulging, cracked, kinked or leaking (the manual says hoses should be replaced every 5 years). A bad smell stays after the monthly clean. The washer needs to be moved, or the room could freeze. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's manual W10432633A for Whirlpool front-loading washer models WFW9351 and WFW9151. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Take the laundry out as soon as the cycle ends.
Leave the door open so the washer can dry. This prevents smells.
Wipe spills on the outside with a soft damp cloth, with mild soap if needed.
Now and then, wipe the inside of the door glass. Residue there can cause drips.
Empty drum. Put one AFFRESH tablet in the drum, or 2/3 cup (160 mL) of liquid chlorine bleach in the bleach compartment. No detergent.
Close the door and drawer. Press POWER, turn the knob to CLEAN WASHER with affresh, press and hold START/PAUSE.
For about 3 minutes the drum turns and the door locks and unlocks: normal. If the Wash light flashes, take out what is in the drum and start again.
Let it finish. If stopped, "Int" shows and the door can take up to 10 minutes to unlock. Then leave the door slightly open.
Pull the drawer out until it stops. Press down on the release lever and pull it straight out.
Lift out the insert. Wash both in warm soapy water, rinse, and dry. Not dishwasher safe.
Put the insert back, line the drawer up with the guides and slide it in.
Pull back the seal and check for stains and small objects.
Wipe stains with a damp cloth and 3/4 cup (177 mL) of liquid chlorine bleach in 1 gallon (3.8 L) of warm water. Leave 5 minutes, wipe dry, leave the door open.
Run the washer only when you are home. Before a long trip, ask property management whether the water taps behind the washer should be turned off.
After a long time unused, run a Normal cycle with half the usual HE detergent and no clothes.

phone.title: Washer Troubleshooting
phone.model: Whirlpool Model WFW9351 or WFW9151 (to confirm)
phone.important: Do not open the washer cabinet or try to repair it. If water is leaking near an electrical outlet, do not touch the washer or the plug.
phone.stop: Water leaks from the washer, the hoses or the door. An error code comes back after you restart, or the washer will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or a loud grinding or banging noise. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's manual W10432633A for Whirlpool front-loading washer models WFW9351 and WFW9151. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Sd: too many suds. Let it carry on. If the knob lights flash, choose the cycle again with a cold temperature and press START/PAUSE. Next time use less HE detergent.
F8 E1: no water. Check both taps behind the washer are on and the hoses are not kinked. Press START/PAUSE once to clear, then again to restart.
F9 E1: cannot drain. Check the drain hose is not kinked or blocked, then clear and restart.
Other F/E code: press POWER. If water is left, run RINSE/DRAIN & SPIN. If it comes back, contact property management.

steps.title: Won't start or door won't open

items.html: Close the door until it latches, then press and hold START/PAUSE. After a cycle, open and close the door first.
Control Lock light on: hold Control Lock (Cycle Signal on some models) for 3 seconds. Check the plug and breaker.

items.cap: From the manufacturer's manual, page 6. Both models are shown.

items.html: Door locked: press START/PAUSE once and wait for the drum to stop. If water is left, run RINSE/DRAIN & SPIN. If TumbleFresh is on, press POWER.
Still wet: run RINSE/DRAIN & SPIN with no detergent. Spread out a tight or one-item load, or take half out and spin again. Delicate cycles leave clothes wetter.
Clicks at the start (door lock), humming while draining, and zips touching the drum are normal.
Shaking: don't wash a single item or pack the drum. Use Bulky Items for comforters. If it still moves, contact property management.
Suds or drips at the door: use only measured HE detergent and wipe the door glass.
Bad smell: run the monthly clean (see Appliance Care) and leave the door open between washes.
Not clean: don't pack the drum, use the dispenser, no softener balls. Grey whites: wash apart from darks, warmer water if the label allows.
Wrinkles: load loosely, slower spin, unload straight away.
Low-looking water, a changing time left, or an option that won't light up for that cycle: all normal.

phone.title: How to Use the Dishwasher
phone.important: Use only automatic dishwasher detergent, never hand dish soap. Load knives and sharp items pointing down. Do not let children play in or on the dishwasher or sit or stand on the open door. Open the door slowly during a cycle: hot water can splash out. Do not touch the heating element at the bottom during or right after a cycle.
phone.stop: Water leaks or pools under the dishwasher. Error code i1 or i4 shows, or it will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or a grinding noise that keeps going. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Use & Care manual A15931101 for this Frigidaire dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.cap: Upper basket. From the manufacturer's manual, page 7.
Lower basket. From the manufacturer's manual, page 7.

items.html: Scrape off large food, bones and toothpicks. Empty glasses and cups. Rinse only if the dishes will wait before washing.
Upper basket: glasses, cups, small plates and plastics marked dishwasher safe. Open side down, tilted slightly.
Lower basket: plates, bowls, pots and pans facing down. Items up to 11 inches tall. Fold the tines down for big pots.

items.cap: Cutlery basket. From the manufacturer's manual, page 8.

items.html: Cutlery basket: knives and sharp items pointing down.
Turn the spray arm under the upper basket by hand: nothing should stop it or block the detergent cup.
If the dishwasher drains into the sink's garbage disposal, run the disposal first so it is empty.
Push the release catch to open the detergent cup.
Add automatic dishwasher detergent, then press the cover down until it closes. The cover is always open again at the end of a cycle: normal.
Rinse aid (liquid only) helps dishes dry. Check the window next to the cup. To fill, lift the tab, fill up to the full mark (not past it), press the cover down. It lasts about a month.
Never put detergent in the rinse aid side, and never use powder or solid rinse aid.

items.cap: Control panel. From the manufacturer's manual, page 5.

items.html: Normal Wash: everyday loads. Heavy Wash: pots, pans, casseroles. 1 Hour Wash: lightly soiled, no drying. China Crystal: delicate china and glass. Energy Saver: lightly soiled, pre-rinsed dishes.
Rinse Only: rinses now so food doesn't dry on until you run a full load. No detergent.
Press Options to choose Sanitize (Heavy and Normal only), High Temp or Heat Dry. A light shows what is on.
Delay: press Delay until the hours (1h to 24h) show, then press START/Cancel.
Control Lock: hold Options and Delay together for 3 seconds. Do the same to unlock.

items.cap: Cycle lights. From the manufacturer's manual, page 6.

items.html: Close the door until it latches and press START/Cancel. The display shows the minutes left. The time can jump up or down: normal.
Cancel: hold START/Cancel for 3 seconds.
Add a dish: open the door a little and wait for the spraying to stop. Add the dish, close the door firmly and press START/Cancel.
At the end it beeps and the Clean light stays on until you open the door (Sanitized if you chose Sanitize). Dishes can be hot.

phone.title: Dishwasher Care
phone.important: Let the heating element at the bottom cool before cleaning inside: burn risk. Do not use benzene, wax, thinner, chlorine bleach or alcohol. Do not spray water over the dishwasher or let water reach electrical parts. Do not remove the long rubber seal around the tub opening.
phone.stop: A filter or the spray arm is broken or will not lock back. The door seal is torn, or the door still does not close properly. Water leaks or pools under the dishwasher. A bad smell stays after the vinegar cycle. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Use & Care manual A15931101 for this Frigidaire dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.cap: Inside the dishwasher. From the manufacturer's manual, page 4.

items.html: Wipe spills as they happen. Soft damp cloth on the control panel. Stainless door: stainless steel cleaner and a soft cloth.
Wipe the inside and the inner door with a wet dishcloth.
Now and then, fill the detergent cup and run it empty on Normal Wash with Sanitize.
White spots or smell: run Normal Wash empty with no detergent. Once water has run through, open the door, put an 8 oz cup of white vinegar upright in the lower basket, close and let it finish.
Turn the dishwasher off and let the heating element cool.
Turn the filter insert counterclockwise and lift it out.
Pull out the flat, rectangular fine filter.
Remove food and rinse the filters under running water.
Put the filters back in reverse order. Turn the insert clockwise to the close arrow. If it is not closed properly, it cleans less well.
Dishes not clean or holes blocked: pull the lower spray arm straight up, gently.
Clear the holes, push it back and spin it by hand to check it turns.
Door not closing well or leaking: wipe the door seal with a damp cloth to remove food.
Check the rinse aid window about once a month. Lift the tab, fill with liquid rinse aid up to the full mark (not past it), press the cover down firmly.

phone.title: Dishwasher Troubleshooting
phone.important: Do not open the dishwasher panels or try to repair it. If water overflows, turn off the water to the dishwasher if you know where the valve is (often under the kitchen sink; property management can confirm) and do not restart it until the water is cleaned up.
phone.stop: Water leaks, overflows or pools under the dishwasher. Code i1 or i4 comes back, or it will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or a grinding noise that keeps going after a full cycle. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Use & Care manual A15931101 for this Frigidaire dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.cap: Control panel with display. From the manufacturer's manual, page 5.

items.html: i1: water takes too long to come in (supply off or low pressure). Contact property management if it happens again.
i4: leaking. Turn it off and contact property management.
Won't start: close the door until it latches. Delay light on: hold START/Cancel 3 seconds to cancel. Controls do nothing: hold Options and Delay 3 seconds (Control Lock). Check the plug and breaker.
Heavy soil and Sanitize make cycles longer. Not-hot incoming water does too: avoid running it during showers. A beep at the end is normal.
Not clean: don't load too close together; make sure the spray arms turn freely; use fresh detergent; choose Heavy Wash for very dirty loads.
Clean the filters (see Appliance Care). Detergent left in the cup: old detergent, or a dish blocked the spray arm.
Wet dishes, spots or film: fill with fresh rinse aid and choose a cycle with drying or Heat Dry.
Black or grey marks: aluminium pans rubbed against dishes. Load them apart.
Reddish tomato stains: run Rinse Only right after loading. Coffee or tea stains: use a dishwasher spot cleaner.
Water left at the bottom: the cycle was stopped. Run a cycle to the end.
Won't drain: run the sink's garbage disposal so it is empty. Still not draining: contact property management.
Suds or leaks: use only automatic dishwasher detergent, never hand dish soap.
Detergent cup and drain pump noises are normal. Grinding means a hard object got in: if it keeps going after a full cycle, contact property management.
Won't fill: close the door fully. If it still won't fill, contact property management.

phone.title: How to Use the Washer
phone.model: LG front-load washer WM5500H*A or WM6500H*A (model to confirm)
phone.important: Use only HE (High-Efficiency) detergent, and less than half the maximum on the bottle for an average load. Pods, gel and tablets go in the drum, never in the drawer. Never mix chlorine bleach with ammonia or vinegar. Do not touch the door during steam cycles: it gets very hot. Keep children and pets out of the drum.
phone.stop: Water leaks or pools under the washer. A message comes back after a restart, or the washer will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or a loud banging or grinding noise. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71964314 for LG washers WM5500H*A and WM6500H*A. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Sort by colour, dirt level and fabric. Wash darks apart from lights.
Empty pockets, close zippers and hooks, tie strings. Small items go in a mesh bag.
Load loosely, large items first. Do not press clothes down: the door must close easily.
Do not wash one small item alone. DO NOT OVERLOAD. Overloading will cause leak.
Waterproof items (rain jackets, mattress covers): use the Bedding cycle only.
Check that nothing hangs over the rubber door seal.

items.cap: 1 Pre-wash (some models), 2 liquid detergent cup, 3 main wash detergent, 4 fabric softener, 5 liquid chlorine bleach. Manual, page 21.

items.html: HE detergent goes in the main wash compartment (3). Liquid: keep the liquid detergent cup (2) in place. Powder: take the cup out first.
Pods, gel or tablets: one only, in the empty drum before the clothes.
Fabric softener (4) and liquid chlorine bleach (5): never past the MAX line. Never more than 1 cup of bleach.
Close the drawer gently. A little water left in it after the wash is normal.
Do not keep detergent or bleach on top of the washer.

items.cap: 1 Power, 2 cycle knob, 3 Back and ✓ (OK), 4 display, 5 Start/Pause, 6 Temp., Spin, Soil, 7 options. Manual, page 23.

items.html: Press Power (1). Turn the knob (2) to a cycle and press ✓ (3).

items.cap: Screen inside the knob: it shows the cycle and settings. Back and ✓ (OK) buttons below. Manual, page 24.

items.html: Normal: cotton, jeans, mixed loads. AI Wash: adjusts to the load. Towels. Heavy Duty. Bedding: comforters and waterproof items. Delicates. Quick Wash: small, lightly soiled loads.
Not sure? Choose Normal for everyday laundry.
Change Temp., Spin and Soil with the buttons (6). Two chimes and no light means that setting is not allowed for this cycle.

items.cap: Temp., Spin and Soil levels light up 1 to 5. Manual, page 25.

items.html: Extra Rinse (1 to 3 rinses), Delay Start (1 to 19 hours), Fresh Care (tumbles for up to 19 hours if you cannot unload right away).
Press Start/Pause (5). The door locks and the drum turns briefly to weigh the load. Start soon after choosing, or the washer turns off.
Seeing very little water is normal for this washer.
Pause: press Start/Pause. Cancel: press Power; the door unlocks after a short pause.
Buttons beep but nothing happens? Control Lock is on. Press Options, turn the knob to Control Lock, press ✓, choose Off, press ✓.
At the end a melody plays. Unload straight away and check the door seal for small items.
Leave the door open so the drum dries.

phone.title: Washer Care
phone.model: LG front-load washer WM5500H*A or WM6500H*A (model to confirm)
phone.important: Wear rubber gloves and goggles when cleaning with bleach, and always dilute it. Never mix chlorine bleach with ammonia or vinegar. Do not spray water on or into the washer. No steel wool, abrasive cleaners, alcohol or solvents. Opening the drain filter lets water out: only do it with towels and a shallow pan ready.
phone.stop: A water hose behind the washer is leaking, kinked or cracked. A bad smell stays after three weekly Tub Clean cycles. The washer shows Water supply with the taps open (the water inlet filters behind it may need cleaning). The room could freeze. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71964314 for LG washers WM5500H*A and WM6500H*A. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Take the laundry out as soon as the cycle ends.
Wipe the door, the door glass and the inside of the rubber seal dry.
Leave the door open, overnight if you can, so the drum dries. This prevents smells. Keep children and pets out.
Wipe spills on the outside straight away with a damp cloth.

items.cap: 1 Power, 2 cycle knob, 3 Back and ✓ (OK), 4 display, 5 Start/Pause, 6 Temp., Spin, Soil, 7 options. Manual, page 23.

items.html: Empty drum. Add a washer drum cleaner to the main detergent compartment, or liquid chlorine bleach to the bleach compartment (not past MAX). Cleaning tablets go in the drum.
Press Power, turn the knob to Tub Clean, press Start/Pause.
No Tub Clean on the knob? Press Options, choose Cycle List Edit, turn to Tub Clean and press ✓ to add it.
Afterwards leave the door open to dry. If you used a cleaner or descaler, run Rinse+Spin (add it the same way) before the next wash.
Smell already there? Run Tub Clean once a week for 3 weeks.

steps.title: Dispenser drawer (once or twice a month)

items.cap: Press the release button (1) to take the drawer out. Manual, page 41.

items.html: Turn off and unplug the washer. Pull the drawer out until it stops.
Press down hard on the release button (1) and pull the drawer all the way out. Take out the inserts.
Clean them with warm water and a soft cloth or brush. No soap. Dry them.
Brush out the drawer opening with a small non-metal brush, then slide the drawer back in.
Wear rubber gloves and goggles. Mix 3/4 cup (177 mL) of liquid chlorine bleach in 1 gallon (3.8 L) of water. Never use bleach undiluted.
Wipe all around the seal with a sponge or soft cloth, then dry it with a towel.
Leave the door open until the seal is completely dry.
Hard water spots on the drum: a soft cloth with stainless steel cleaner. Then run Tub Clean.

items.cap: Open the drain filter cover at the bottom front. Manual, page 43.

items.html: Turn off and unplug the washer. Put towels and a shallow pan on the floor.
Open the drain filter cover. Unclip the small drain hose, pull out its plug and let the water run into the pan.
Twist the filter counterclockwise to take it out. Remove lint, coins and other objects.

items.cap: Twist to remove the filter. Manual, page 43.

items.html: Put the plug back in the hose and clip it. Twist the filter clockwise until tight. Close the cover.
Still won't drain, or water keeps coming out: contact property management.

phone.title: Washer Troubleshooting
phone.model: LG front-load washer WM5500H*A or WM6500H*A (model to confirm)
phone.important: Water leaking, or the message Water too high: stop using the washer, turn off its water taps if you know where they are, and contact property management right away.
phone.stop: Water leaks. Water too high, No water detected, Vibration sensor, Steam error, No temp detected or Voltage abnormality. Motor error after waiting 30 minutes. A message comes back after a restart. A burning smell or smoke. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71964314 for LG washers WM5500H*A and WM6500H*A. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Press Power, choose a cycle, close the door fully, then press Start/Pause. If you wait too long after choosing, the washer turns off.
Buttons beep but nothing happens? Control Lock is on. Press Options, turn the knob to Control Lock, press ✓, choose Off, press ✓.
Door open or Door unlocked: open and close the door. Check nothing is caught in the seal.
Display stays dark: the breaker may be off. A washer left in the cold must warm up first.
Power failure: press Start/Pause to restart.
Water supply: the water taps may not be fully open, or a hose is kinked. Contact property management.
Unbalance: load too small or tangled. Pause, spread the clothes out, or add a few similar items.
Oversudsing: too much detergent. The washer removes suds for about 2 hours. Use less HE detergent next time.
Motor error: wait 30 minutes and restart.
Drainage: clean the drain filter (see Appliance Care), or contact property management.
Freeze error: contact property management.
Clicking, hissing, humming, sloshing: normal.
Rattling: coins or keys. Check the drum and the drain filter (see Appliance Care).
Thumping or shaking: pause and spread the load out.
Stops for a few minutes, then restarts: motor protection, normal. Time left is only an estimate.
Musty smell: run Tub Clean, clean the door seal and drain filter, leave the door open, use less HE detergent.
Detergent left in the drawer: close it fully before starting, and do not overfill.

phone.title: How to Use the Dryer
phone.model: LG dryer, DL*X550, DL*X650 or DL*X670 series (model to confirm)
phone.important: Clean the lint filter before every load, and never run the dryer without it. Never dry anything with gasoline, cleaning solvents or cooking oil on it, or anything with foam rubber, rubber or plastic. Do not touch the door or reach in during steam cycles. Keep children and pets out of the drum.
phone.stop: A burning smell or smoke (a light smell on the very first use is normal). The Duct blockage message, or clothes take much longer than usual to dry. The dryer does not heat. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71996102 for LG dryers DL*X550, DL*X650 and DL*X670. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.cap: Lint filter (1): pull it straight up. Manual, page 49.

items.html: Pull the lint filter (1) straight up, roll the lint off with your fingers, and push it back until it clicks.
Load loosely: clothes grow as they dry. Push everything fully inside, away from the door seal.
Tie strings and belts. Items with zippers or hooks go in a mesh bag.
Dry heavy items apart from light ones, and follow the care labels.
Never dry bath mats, rubber, plastic or fibreglass items.

items.cap: 1 Power, 2 cycle knob, 3 Back and ✓ (OK), 4 display, 5 Start/Pause, 6 Temp., Dry Level, Dry Time, 7 options. Manual, page 33.

items.html: Press Power (1). Turn the knob (2) to a cycle.
Normal: cotton, jeans, mixed loads. AI Dry: adjusts to the load. Bedding: comforters, pillows. Delicates: blouses, lingerie.
Not sure? Choose Normal for everyday laundry.
Change Temp., Dry Level and Dry Time with the buttons (6).
Energy Saver is on by default in Normal: the cycle starts with no heat, which is normal. Wrinkle Care tumbles the clothes for up to 3 hours after the cycle.
Press Start/Pause (5). Start soon after choosing, or the dryer turns off and the settings are lost.
To pause, open the door or press Start/Pause.
Buttons beep but nothing happens? Control Lock is on. Press Options, turn the knob to Control Lock, press ✓, choose Off, press ✓.
A chime sounds at the end. Unload straight away to avoid wrinkles. With Wrinkle Care on, the dryer turns by itself every few minutes: normal. Turn the dryer off before unloading.
Very small load: add a few items so the dryer can sense when it is dry.
One bulky comforter: pause once or twice and unroll it so the middle dries.
Wool: follow the label. If still damp, do not repeat the cycle: lay it flat to finish.
Steam options: not for wool, silk or delicate fabrics. Water drips and a drum that stops during steam are normal.

phone.title: Dryer Care
phone.model: LG dryer, DL*X550, DL*X650 or DL*X670 series (model to confirm)
phone.important: Turn off and unplug the dryer before cleaning it. Never use harsh chemicals, solvents, steel wool or abrasive cleaners. Never run the dryer without the lint filter in place.
phone.stop: Lint builds up behind the dryer or around the outside vent, the Duct blockage message shows, or the Flow Sense indicator shows 4 bars: the vent duct needs cleaning (the manual says check it monthly and clean it at least once a year). A burning smell. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71996102 for LG dryers DL*X550, DL*X650 and DL*X670. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Before every load, open the door and pull the filter straight up.

items.cap: Roll the lint off with your fingers. Manual, page 49.

items.html: Roll the lint off with your fingers, or vacuum it.
Push it back in firmly until it clicks.

items.cap: Wash a clogged filter in warm, soapy water. Manual, page 50.

items.html: Hold the clean filter up to a light. If it looks dirty or clogged with fabric softener, wash it in warm, soapy water.
Let it dry completely before putting it back.
Very linty loads, like new towels: pause the cycle and clean the filter halfway.
Outside: warm water with a mild, non-abrasive detergent. Wipe spills straight away.
Door opening and seal: wipe with a soft damp cloth to remove lint and dust.
Door window: a soft cloth with warm soapy water, then wipe dry.
Drum: a stainless steel cleaner, following its label.
Vacuum lint and dust from around and under the dryer regularly.
If drying gets slower or air seems weak, tell property management: the vent duct may be blocked.
Do not keep anything flammable on or near the dryer.

phone.title: Dryer Troubleshooting
phone.model: LG dryer, DL*X550, DL*X650 or DL*X670 series (model to confirm)
phone.important: Duct blockage (80%, 90% or 95%): stop using the dryer. The manual warns that running it with a blocked vent is dangerous and could cause a fire. Contact property management.
phone.stop: Duct blockage, Temp sensor error, or a Power supply, Power issue or voltage message. A burning smell or smoke. No heat after checking the boxes below. Steam does not work. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual MFL71996102 for LG dryers DL*X550, DL*X650 and DL*X670. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Press Power, choose a cycle, close the door, press Start/Pause. If you wait too long after choosing, the dryer turns off.
Buttons beep but nothing happens? Control Lock is on. Press Options, turn the knob to Control Lock, press ✓, choose Off, press ✓.
Nothing lights up: the breaker may be off. Contact property management.
Starts by itself every few minutes after the cycle: that is Wrinkle Care. Normal.
Clean the lint filter before every load. Wash it if it looks clogged (see Appliance Care).
Do not overload. Very small load: add a few items.
Dry heavy items apart from light ones. Unroll a bulky comforter halfway through.
No heat at the start of Normal: Energy Saver is on. Normal; you can turn it off.
Flow Sense shows 4 bars: the vent is partly blocked. Contact property management.
Duct blockage: see the IMPORTANT box.
Temp sensor error: turn the dryer off and contact property management.
Power supply, Power issue, High voltage or Low voltage: contact property management.
Wrinkles: unload right away, use a shorter time or lower Dry Level, or use Wrinkle Care.
Static: shorter drying, fabric softener, or Low Static.
Lint on clothes: clean the filter, dry towels apart from dark clothes. Check pockets for tissues.
Shrinking: follow care labels, use a low heat setting.
Steam: water drips, no visible steam, or a drum that stops: normal.
New dryer smell: normal, goes away after a few cycles.

phone.title: How to Use the Dishwasher
phone.model: KitchenAid dishwasher, stainless steel tub (model to confirm)
phone.important: Use only dishwasher detergent and keep it away from children. Load sharp knives with the handles up. Do not sit or stand on the door or racks, do not push down on the open door, and do not let children play in or on the dishwasher. Do not touch the heating element during or right after a cycle.
phone.stop: Water leaks or pools under the dishwasher. An error code shows or the lights blink in a pattern (see Troubleshooting). A burning smell or smoke. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual W11589935 for this KitchenAid dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Load sharp knives with the handles up.
Place sharp items so they cannot touch or damage the door seal.
Plastic: only items marked dishwasher safe.
Do not sit, stand or lean on the open door or the racks.
Use only dishwasher detergent. Premeasured tablets or packs are recommended.
Rinse aid is needed for dry dishes and to limit hard-water spots. Keep it filled.
The detergent cup and rinse aid cap are on the inside of the door (location to confirm with property management).
Choose a cycle on the control panel, for example Normal. Not sure which one? Ask property management.
Press Start/Resume, then close the door within 4 seconds.
Start/Resume light flashing: the door was not closed in time. Press Start/Resume again and close the door.
Adding a dish during a cycle: add it, press Start/Resume and close the door within 4 seconds.
A load usually takes 2 to 5 hours. This is normal: it saves energy.
The first cycle may run longer. Some options can make a cycle longer than 3.5 hours.
Hot water not used for 2 weeks or more? Before using the dishwasher, run every hot tap for a few minutes. No smoking or open flame while you do this (hydrogen gas risk).

phone.title: Dishwasher Care
phone.model: KitchenAid dishwasher, stainless steel tub (model to confirm)
phone.important: Do not touch the heating element during or right after a cycle. Never use a wire brush or scouring pad on the filters, or abrasive cleaners on the outside. Use vinegar only now and then: it is an acid and can damage the dishwasher.
phone.stop: A filter is broken or will not go back in place. Water leaks or pools under the dishwasher. The dishwasher is not draining well. White residue keeps coming back after cleaning. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual W11589935 for this KitchenAid dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Outside: soft damp cloth and mild detergent only. No abrasive cleaners (stainless doors may have a fingerprint-resistant coating).
Once a month: run a dishwasher cleaner such as affresh®, following the package directions.
White residue: place (do not pour) 2 cups (500 mL) white vinegar in a glass or dishwasher-safe cup on the bottom rack. Run a full cycle with an air-dry or energy-saving dry option and no detergent.
How often: every 2 months if you only scrape plates; every 4 months to once a year if you rinse them first. White residue (hard water): once a month.

items.cap: Turn the upper filter. From the manufacturer's manual, page 5.

items.html: Turn the upper filter 1/4 turn counterclockwise and lift it out.
Gently pull the upper filter assembly apart.
Rinse the filters under running water until most soil is gone.
Hard soil or white deposits: use a soft brush.

items.cap: Scan for the manufacturer's video on putting the filter back. From the manual, page 6.

items.html: Put the filters back fully before the next cycle.
Keep rinse aid filled for dry dishes.

items.cap: Salt reservoir, under the lower rack on the left. From the manufacturer's manual, page 5.

items.html: Low-salt light (some models): refill with dishwasher softener salt only. Remove the lower rack, unscrew the cap, fill to the edge with the funnel, wipe away salt and screw the cap on tightly. Run a cycle right away. Unsure? Contact property management.
Away for a long time, or risk of freezing: tell property management.

phone.title: Dishwasher Troubleshooting
phone.model: KitchenAid dishwasher, stainless steel tub (model to confirm)
phone.important: Water leaking or overfilling (codes F1E1, F1E5, F8E4, F8E5): keep the door closed. Turn off the water to the dishwasher if you know how. If the water cannot be turned off, do NOT turn off the power. Press Cancel once to stop the alarm, then contact property management right away.
phone.stop: Water leaks, overflows or pools under the dishwasher. Any code other than H2O, or H2O comes back. It will not drain. A burning smell or smoke. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
phone.footer: Based on the manufacturer's Owner's Manual W11589935 for this KitchenAid dishwasher. Pictures are taken from that manual.

items.html: Close the door tightly until it latches.
Press Start/Resume, then close the door within 4 seconds. Light flashing: press Start/Resume again and close the door.
Check that a cycle was chosen.
Still nothing: the breaker or water may be off. Contact property management.
2 to 5 hours is normal. The first cycle and some options take longer.
Wet dishes: fill the rinse aid.

items.cap: Upper filter. From the manufacturer's manual, page 5.

items.html: White spots or residue: hard water. Clean the filters monthly and run a dishwasher cleaner or vinegar rinse (see Appliance Care). Tell property management if it continues.
H2O: no water reaching the dishwasher. Contact property management to check the water supply. When it is fixed, press Start/Resume.
F9E1: will not drain. Contact property management (the drain hose or disposal connection may need checking).
F1E1, F1E5, F8E4, F8E5: follow the IMPORTANT box above.
F1E2, F6E1, F7E2, F7E3, F9E3: the dishwasher needs service. Contact property management.
No display? The same faults show as blinking lights, for example 8 blinks, pause, 1 blink = H2O. Count the blinks and tell property management.
Press Cancel once to stop an alarm sound.
